status: User accepted the 1 exact diagnostic sites on 2026-10-07. Focused qualification and its recorded limits are unchanged. Full RPM and native architecture qualification remain separate gates.
root_cause: The compiler diagnoses a possible failed fast allocation following EnsureAllocation in the aligned slow helper. This helper is not selected by production allocation: upstream defines USE_ALLOCATION_ALIGNMENT_BOOL false, and the only caller chooses AllocateRawSlowUnaligned. The exact candidate-7 object disassembly confirms the unaligned target.
source_review: Upstream disables allocation alignment explicitly in globals.h, citing its known alignment inconsistency. This packaging adds no disabling flag or source change.
The only source call to AllocateRawSlowAligned is the false compile-time branch in AllocateRawSlow. AllocateRaw similarly selects its unaligned fast path.

For directly exercised aligned controls, semispace reserves actual filler plus object size; paged space reserves maximum filler. ComputeLimit preserves the minimum request even with observers. No intervening allocation occurs before AllocateFastAligned.

This capacity proof is not generalized to PagedNewSpace fallback paths: those pass the raw size to TryAllocatePage/WaitForSweepingForAllocation. Upstream explicitly leaves aligned allocation inactive. Qualification does not enable or certify a changed upstream alignment policy.

coverage.matrix: 4/8-byte tagged sizes, all three alignment modes, five object sizes, eight/four aligned starting offsets, runtime/GC origin tags, modeled semispace/paged capacity contracts, observer limits, reservation failure, direct fast-path failure and null output pointer. Debug/release normally and under Valgrind.
coverage.memory: All four native memory runs have zero errors and all allocations freed.
coverage.actual_node: Inspector allocation sampling verifies emitted positive samples while arrays, doubles, strings and objects survive garbage collection. Tests run with semispace, forced slow allocation/stress marking, and paged minor collection.
coverage.production_object: Candidate-7 main-allocator.o: AllocateRawSlow dispatches to AllocateRawSlowUnaligned; full disassembly excerpt retained.

limits: The 8-byte-tag release control reproduces the exact warning twice (the helper and its inlined copy). Other modes emit no warning. Exact aligned fast/slow bodies and alignment helpers use typed heap/area adapters.
Actual JavaScript checks exercise production allocation and observers. They do not exercise the inactive aligned helper; this distinction is central to the qualification.

The initial adapter made ToAddress always check failure. It was corrected to match upstream debug-only checking before final qualification; final 8-byte-tag release controls then reproduce the diagnostic.
Native EnsureAllocation models the reviewed semispace/paged minimum-capacity contracts; it does not implement the complete heap policies or certify inactive paged-new-space fallback behavior.
Unused origin parameters in unchanged helper bodies use the same unused-parameter flag as the production build; no uninitialized-warning suppression is applied.
No runtime patch, suppression, allocation policy or compiler-flag change is proposed.
